pages.text: Focus enough light into a small enough spot and it collapses into a black hole (the hoop conjecture). Then the hard part: a micro black hole evaporates faster the smaller it is, so it must be fed exactly as fast as it radiates - an unstable balance.
$(thing)Set$(): Pulse energy, Photon energy, Numerical aperture, Feed rate ṁ.$(br2)$(thing)Disturbance$(): Feed-coupling efficiency drifts: only ṁ·(1 + 5%·d) actually falls in.
$(thing)Limits$(): Hoop conjecture not met: the pulse is not focused inside its own Schwarzschild radius.$(br2)$(thing)Rate$(): The chamber works at a fixed pace once the hole is in range.

$(thing)Equations$()$(br)Pulse mass E/c²: M = E/c²$(br)Schwarzschild radius (pulse): r_s = 2GM/c²$(br)Focal spot radius: r = λ/(2·NA)$(br)Black hole mass: log₁₀ M$(br)Hawking temperature: T_H = ħc³/(8πGMk)$(br)Hawking power: P = ħc⁶/(15360πG²M²)$(br)Equilibrium feed: ṁ_eq = P/c²
